listing_view.reasoning: Subscription ran to 88.8x by close on the final day, after a slow start (0.44x on day one) — that is strong, if heavily last-minute, demand. The cap price implies a P/E of 13.7 against the document's own 18.31 benchmark (0.75x), so the band leaves room on paper. But I have no grey-market premium, no anchor book, and no category-wise split of that 88x, so part of the demand picture is unobservable.

longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue grew 28.8% over two years and the order book of ₹12,047 million [business, page 245] covers roughly 2.7x latest-year revenue, which is genuine forward visibility. Against that: ROCE has fallen from 47.5% to 28.8%, margins only recovered to below the oldest year's level, latest-year operating cash flow is negative ₹121 million while paper profit is ₹433 million, and total debt rose 59% in the latest year. Profitable growth that consumes cash is worth materially less than the P&L suggests.

governance.reasoning: The document prints a debt-to-equity of 0.23 where our own arithmetic on the same numbers gives 1.18 — a 5x discrepancy in a headline solvency ratio in the issuer's own document is a serious red flag regardless of which figure is right. Promoters have extended unsecured loans to the company and stand to be repaid with interest [promoters, page 325], there is an open show-cause notice from the commercial taxes department [litigation, page 445], and director guarantees back company facilities [promoters, page 358, page 432]. No fraud is proven; the standard of disclosure is the concern.

key_risks.risk: Profits are not converting to cash
key_risks.why_it_matters: Latest-year operating cash flow is negative against ₹433m of PAT, so earnings quality, not just growth, is in question.
The printed 0.23 cannot be reproduced from the statement figures (our sum: 1.18); an unreconciled solvency ratio undermines trust in all printed ratios.
ROCE fell from 47.5% to 28.8% over two years while debt rose 59%, suggesting incremental growth is being bought with cheaper returns and more leverage.
Promoters are creditors via unsecured loans and company facilities are secured by director guarantees, so listed-company cash flows partly service promoter interests.
A September 2023 notice from the Department of Commercial Taxes is unresolved at filing, an unquantified contingent liability.

key_risks.risk: Contract-execution risk on a large order book
key_risks.why_it_matters: The company itself flags that inability to recover cost escalations or time overruns hurts financials — relevant when the order book is ~2.7x annual revenue.

answers.question: where did the money go — receivables, inventory, or both?
answers.answer: Not receivables: receivable days collapsed from 94 to 19.5, so customers are paying far faster than before and receivables cannot be the latest-year cash drain. By elimination the negative operating cash flow (against rising revenue) points to inventory/contract-asset build, i.e. working capital tied up in executing the growing order book — but no inventory or working-capital breakdown was given to me, so I cannot confirm that from these extracts. Causal identification is therefore incomplete.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A reconciliation of the printed 0.23 debt-to-equity against the balance sheet, and a working-capital note showing whether the cash outflow is inventory or contract assets, would move the longterm score decisively up (if explained) or down (if not). Category-wise subscription data showing retail/HNI quality rather than a QIB-heavy last-day spike would refine the listing view.
